name: PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (UG)
notes: Source: official PM-USP CSSS guidelines (Department of Higher Education, 6 Feb 2024 version, read directly) and the myScheme page https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/csss-cus, which agree. Amount: Rs 12,000 a year for years 1-3; B.Tech/B.E. students get Rs 20,000 in year 4 (amount field holds the year 1-3 rate). Merit rule not encodable: applicant must be above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in their stream and Board in Class 12, so no marks criterion is set and this is NOT checked by the engine. Other conditions not encoded: regular (not correspondence/distance) course at an AICTE-recognised institution; renewal needs at least 50% marks and 75% attendance; Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Excludes diploma students (course_level limited to UG). Students already getting any other scholarship, including State scholarship or fee waiver/reimbursement schemes, are not eligible, hence exclusive_with. caste_certificate applies to reserved categories only; disability_certificate only if applicable. Application window not set: NSP publishes timelines and the 2026-27 window was not confirmed.

name: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
notes: Source: myScheme (Govt of India), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Amount shown is Group 1 (degree and post-graduate professional courses): Rs 10,000 academic allowance plus Rs 10,000 tuition fee. Other groups pay Rs 13,000, Rs 8,000 and Rs 5,000. Income ceiling is Rs 2.5 lakh a year (parents'/guardians' income, or combined income for employed students). Open to OBC, EBC and DNT students as notified for the applicant's own State; the profile has only an OBC category, so EBC and DNT students are not matched. Only two boys of the same parents can receive it (this limit does not apply to girls), not encoded. A holder may not hold another scholarship or stipend and must choose one; exclusive_with lists the other central scheme in this file. Domicile/permanent settlement in the State is required but not encoded. Application window not confirmed. CONFLICT, confidence lowered: the SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26" (listed at https://ssp.karnataka.gov.in/Downloads), Backward Classes Welfare section, gives different rules for Karnataka: income up to Rs 2.5 lakh for Category-1 but only Rs 1 lakh for other OBC categories (2A, 3A, 3B); minimum marks 60 per cent (Category-1) or 70 per cent (others); not for management, private or COMED-K seats, or students already getting fee concession or the NT/SNT scholarship. These are not encoded: the profile has no OBC sub-category, and 2026-27 rules were not seen.

name: Karnataka SSP: Fee reimbursement for SC students in post-matric courses (family income below Rs 2.5 lakh)
notes: Source: Karnataka Social Welfare Department education page (Kannada; translated; undated), post-matric scholarship section; the scheme was first read from the State Scholarship Portal scheme list. No single yearly amount exists, so amount is null: the department pays the compulsory non-refundable fees, which vary by course, plus a maintenance allowance that varies by group (day scholar / hosteller): Group I degree and PG professional Rs 7,000 / 13,500; Group II Rs 6,500 / 9,500; Group III Rs 3,000 / 6,000; Group IV Rs 2,500 / 4,000. The page says this is a centrally sponsored programme, so it is the same benefit as central-post-matric-sc. Marked exclusive with PM-USP because PM-USP excludes students who already get State fee reimbursement. Checked against the SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26" (listed at https://ssp.karnataka.gov.in/Downloads), Social Welfare section: SC, family income less than or equal to Rs 2.5 lakh, all courses; it lists RD-numbered caste and income certificates (and Aadhaar, not recorded here). It states no amount and no domicile rule, so no state criterion is set.

name: Karnataka SSP: Fee reimbursement for SC students in technical, medical and AYUSH courses (family income Rs 2.5-10 lakh)
notes: Amount: the Karnataka Social Welfare Department education page (Kannada; translated; undated) says engineering and medical students with family income from Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh get a 50 per cent fee concession from the Technical and Medical Education departments. It is a share of the course fee, not a fixed figure, so amount is null; AYUSH is not mentioned there. Other conditions below come from the Karnataka State Scholarship Portal scheme list, Social Welfare Department (Kannada; translated). Stated conditions: SC students in technical, medical or AYUSH courses with annual family income above Rs 2.5 lakh and below Rs 10 lakh. The course type (technical/medical/AYUSH) is not encoded because the profile 'course' field is free text; Documents, domicile rule and dates are not stated on either page (docs empty, no state criterion). Marked exclusive with PM-USP for the same reason as the other Karnataka fee reimbursement. The income band follows the SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26" (listed at https://ssp.karnataka.gov.in/Downloads): above Rs 2.5 lakh and up to and including Rs 10 lakh, professional courses. That document says the details of this scheme will be published later.

name: Karnataka SSP: Tuition fee reimbursement for SC students in professional courses under management or private quota
notes: Source: Karnataka State Scholarship Portal scheme list, Social Welfare Department (Kannada; translated). The page says only: tuition fee reimbursement for SC students studying professional courses under the management quota or private quota. No income limit is shown there, and the quota condition cannot be checked from the profile, so the engine treats every SC student as matching on category alone. Low confidence: read the full scheme notice before showing this to a student. Amount, documents and dates are not stated on that page.

name: Karnataka SSP: Hostel maintenance cost for SC students in hostels run by technical and medical colleges
notes: Source: Karnataka State Scholarship Portal scheme list, Social Welfare Department (Kannada; translated). The page says only: hostel maintenance cost for SC students living in hostels managed by colleges that run technical and medical courses. Living in such a hostel cannot be checked from the profile, so category is the only criterion; a student who does not live in a college-run hostel will still see this as a match. Low confidence: read the full scheme notice first. Amount, documents, income limit and dates are not stated on that page. The SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26" (listed at https://ssp.karnataka.gov.in/Downloads) lists a Hostel Fee scheme for SC students covering department-run, college or university-run and grant-in-aid hostels, with no amount; it does not limit it to technical and medical colleges.

name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for Girl Students (Degree)
notes: Source: AICTE guidelines for the Pragati Scholarship Scheme for Girl Students (Degree), dated July 2020 (academic year 2020-21), read directly from the PDF on the National Scholarship Portal. These are the only guidelines on NSP for the degree scheme; confidence is lowered because they are from 2020 and no 2026-27 eligibility guideline was seen. Eligibility: girl admitted to first year of a degree course, or second year through lateral entry, in an AICTE-approved institution; maximum two girl children per family; family income from all sources not above Rs 8 lakh a year with a State/UT income certificate. year_of_study <= 2 stands in for first year or second-year lateral entry, so a regular second-year student may show a false match. Amount Rs 50,000 a year, for up to 4 years (3 for lateral entry). Only 5,000 awards a year, with Karnataka's allocation at 398; selection is by merit of 10+2 marks, which the engine does not check, so eligible means eligible to apply, not selected. A student may not receive any other scholarship, stipend or emolument from any source, hence exclusive_with lists every other scholarship in this file. A gap of more than two years between the qualifying exam and admission makes a student ineligible (not encoded). Reserved-category students need their category certificate. Dates: AICTE notification of 19.06.2026 says the 2026-27 portal had opened (opens is that notice date) with last date 31.10.2026; a later AICTE notification extends student applications to 30.11.2026 (institute verification to 15.12.2026).

name: AICTE Saksham Scholarship Scheme for Specially-abled Students (Degree)
notes: Source: AICTE guidelines for the Saksham Scholarship Scheme (Degree), July 2020 (2020-21), and the AICTE Saksham FAQ, both read directly. Eligibility: specially-abled student with disability of not less than 40%; admitted to first year of a degree course, or second year through lateral entry, in an AICTE-approved institution; family income from all sources not more than Rs 8 lakh (the guidelines say 'not more than' and the FAQ says 'less than', so exactly Rs 8 lakh is uncertain). The profile's disability field only records whether the student has a disability certificate, so the 40% threshold is not checked. year_of_study <= 2 stands in for first year or second-year lateral entry; the FAQ says a third-year student is not eligible. Amount Rs 50,000 a year for up to 4 years (3 for lateral entry). All eligible applicants get it (no merit cap stated). A student may not receive any other Central, State or AICTE scholarship, so exclusive_with lists every other scholarship in this file. Guidelines are from 2020; 2026-27 eligibility notice not seen. Dates: AICTE notification of 19.06.2026 says the 2026-27 portal had opened (opens is that notice date) with last date 31.10.2026; a later AICTE notification extends student applications to 30.11.2026 (institute verification to 15.12.2026).

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students (Centrally Sponsored)
notes: Source: guidelines of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, March 2021, for 2020-21 to 2025-26 (saved file data/Postmatric_SC.pdf, scanned; pages 1-9 read). WARNING: the guidelines' stated validity ended with 2025-26 and no 2026-27 renewal was seen, so confidence is lowered. source_url is the ministry's page for this scheme, found by web search; it returned 503 Service Unavailable on 2026-11-26 and was not opened. The Karnataka Social Welfare Department page https://swd.karnataka.gov.in/44/education/kn (undated) shows the same Group I allowance of Rs 7,000 / 13,500. Eligibility: SC as notified for the State the student belongs to; passed matriculation or higher; parents'/guardians' income from all sources not above Rs 2.5 lakh in the last financial year; recognised institution. Seats filled through management, NRI or spot quota are not eligible (not encoded). A holder may not keep another scholarship or stipend. Amount is only the Group 1 (degree professional course) day-scholar academic allowance of Rs 7,000 (Rs 13,500 for hostellers); compulsory non-refundable fees are also paid and are not counted, so the real value is higher. Applied through the State's portal. Probably the same benefit that Karnataka SSP delivers as SC fee reimbursement, so these are marked exclusive to avoid double counting.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (Centrally Sponsored)
notes: Source: Ministry of Tribal Affairs guidelines, applicable from 01-04-2022 (saved file 'Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for ST Students_scheme.pdf', read directly). source_url is the ministry's own PDF link; its size on the server matches the saved file exactly (612,474 bytes). Eligibility: ST as specified for the student's domicile State; passed matriculation or higher; family income from all sources not above Rs 2.5 lakh a year (income test does not apply to an orphan supported by a guardian); recognised institution; not getting any other scholarship. Students in the Ministry's listed Top Class institutes are covered by a different scheme instead (not encoded). Amount is only the Group I day-scholar stipend of Rs 5,500 a year (Rs 12,000 for hostellers); compulsory non-refundable fees are also paid (Government of India support capped at Rs 2.5 lakh a year for engineering in private institutes) and are not counted. Applied through the State's portal. For Karnataka, the SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26" (listed at https://ssp.karnataka.gov.in/Downloads), Tribal Welfare section, says private and management seat applications are not eligible (not encoded).

name: Karnataka SSP: Post-matric fee reimbursement for minority students
notes: Source: SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26", listed on the downloads page in source_url (no direct file link exists). Minority Welfare section: Muslim, Christian, Jain, Sikh, Parsi and Buddhist students; resident of Karnataka; at least 50 per cent in the previous year with all subjects passed (backlogs not checked). Income limit is Rs 2.5 lakh for professional and PG degree courses but only Rs 2 lakh for PUC and general degree courses; Rs 2.5 lakh is encoded, so a general degree student between Rs 2 lakh and Rs 2.5 lakh shows a false match. Students of residential colleges are not eligible (not checked). No amount is stated. Deadline: the State Scholarship Portal home page showed 30/11/2026 as this department's last date for FY 2026-27 (read 2026-11-26); no opening date was shown, so application_window is not set. The eligibility rules are from FY 2025-26; FY 2026-27 rules were not seen.

name: Karnataka SSP: Technical Education fee reimbursement for ST students (family income Rs 2.5-10 lakh)
notes: Source: SSP document "Postmatric Scholarship: Eligibility criteria document for FY 2025-26", listed on the downloads page in source_url (no direct file link exists). Department of Technical Education section: ST students with family income above Rs 2.5 lakh and below Rs 10 lakh, in BE/B.Tech, B.Arch, ME/M.Tech, M.Arch or polytechnic diploma courses, admitted through KEA-CET or COMED-K. Course and admission route are not checked, so an ST student in another course shows a false match. No amount or domicile rule is stated. Deadline: the State Scholarship Portal home page showed 30/11/2026 as this department's last date for FY 2026-27 (read 2026-11-26); no opening date was shown, so application_window is not set. The eligibility rules are from FY 2025-26; FY 2026-27 rules were not seen.
